prs.title: Preview: Only pause DocumentTimeline animations in preview-web
prs.manualTesting:
1. Check out this branch and run `yarn nx run-many -t compile`
2. Run the internal Storybook with `cd code && yarn storybook:ui`
3. Open `preview/Animations`:
   - `FadeIn`: the content is visible and not mid-fade.
   - `Infinite`: the rotation is frozen on its first frame, not spinning.
   - `Scroll`: scrolling the story moves the red progress bar. On `next` the bar is stuck at full width because the scroll-timeline animation was snapped to its end.
   - `Transition`: the focused button is fully blue, not mid-transition.
4. For the original report, run the repro from #31877 and confirm the button is visible.

issues.title: [Bug]: pausing animations indiscriminately breaks view-, and scroll-timeline animations

prs.title: UI: Rebuild Sidebar Tree
prs.manualTesting:
1. `cd code && yarn storybook:ui`
2. Navigate the sidebar with the keyboard: arrows move, Enter/Space toggle branches and select stories, the chevron buttons toggle without selecting, ctrl/⌘+shift+U opens the row actions menu for the focused row.
3. Scroll a large expanded tree: ancestor rows stick to the top, clicking a sticky row scrolls its real row into place.
4. Hover the tree: indent lines appear, and the hovered or focused row's own lines take the accent colour. The children of the selected story's parent keep one line visible even when the tree is not hovered.
5. Compose a ref (`refs` in `main.ts`) and confirm the ref tree expands, selects, and scrolls within its own section.
6. Check status icons and the filter panel with a test provider (addon-vitest) running.

prs.title: Tooling: Use pkg.pr.new for canary releases
prs.manualTesting:
Do this **outside** the Storybook monorepo. Yarn in this repo intercepts `npx` and will not exercise the canary CLI.

Wait until the **Canary Release** heading on this PR says Released. Copy the two `npx` commands from that section. Run each command as its own shell invocation (do not chain them after `npx storybook@latest` in one line). On npm 12, keep `--allow-remote=all`.

What should change: Storybook dependencies in `package.json` must be `https://pkg.pr.new/...` URLs with the same SHA as the command. The bug this PR fixes is the canary CLI installing ordinary npm versions such as `10.6.0-alpha.7`.

prs.title: UI: Fix controls expander and select chevron overlap in RTL
prs.manualTesting:
1. Run the internal Storybook (`cd code && yarn storybook:ui`) or a sandbox.
2. **Args table section row:** open *addons/docs → blocks → components → ArgsTable → SectionRow → Section Rtl* and *Collapsed Rtl*. The chevron sits inside the cell on the inline-start (right) edge, the outer corners of the row are rounded, and there is no seam in the middle of the row. Compare with *Section* and *Collapsed* — it is a clean mirror.
3. **Select control:** open *components → Form → Select → Rtl*. The dropdown chevron sits on the inline-end (left) side, clear of the value text.
4. Optionally, in any story with an args table, run `document.documentElement.dir = 'rtl'` in the preview DevTools console. Arg names line up on the right with the same indent as on the left in LTR, and the select controls lay out correctly.

issues.title: [Bug]: Storybook UI controls and table category chevrons overlap text when dir="rtl" is applied globally

prs.title: Core: Accept legacy addon namespaces in CSF factories
prs.manualTesting:
1. In a React Storybook project using CSF factories, register a third-party addon whose `/preview` entry is imported as a namespace.
2. Run `npx storybook automigrate csf-factories`.
3. Run the project's TypeScript check and confirm the generated `definePreview({ addons: [...] })` configuration no longer collapses decorators, render functions, and parameters to `never`.
4. Start Storybook and confirm the third-party preview annotations are still composed at runtime.

prs.title: Core: Replace preview storySort with chained storySorts in main
prs.manualTesting:
1. Generate a sandbox: `yarn task sandbox --template react-vite/default-ts --start-from auto`.
2. In the sandbox's `.storybook/main.ts`, add `storySorts: [{ order: ['Example', ['Header', '*']] }]`.
3. Start Storybook and confirm that the sidebar lists `Example/Header` first.
4. Change it to `storySorts: [{ order: ['Configure your project'] }, { method: 'alphabetical' }]` and restart.
   Confirm that the docs page comes first and the remaining entries are alphabetical.
5. Remove `storySorts` from main and add `parameters: { options: { storySort: { order: ['Example', ['Page', '*']] } } }` to `.storybook/preview.ts`.
   Restart and confirm that the sidebar is in import order.
6. Run `npx storybook automigrate story-sort-to-main` and accept.
   Confirm that `.storybook/main.ts` now has `storySorts: [{ order: ['Example', ['Page', '*']] }]` and that the preview no longer mentions `storySort`.
7. Revert both files, add `storySorts: [{ order: ['Other'] }]` to main as well, and run the command again.
   Confirm that the command reports that main already defines storySorts and that neither file changed.

issues.title: Move storySort from preview.js to main.js

prs.title: Addon A11y: Fix vision simulator color filters in Firefox
prs.manualTesting:
**This needs verifying in Firefox specifically, which CI does not cover.**

1. Build and start the internal Storybook:
   ```bash
   yarn nx run-many -t compile
   cd code && yarn storybook:ui
   ```
2. Open http://localhost:6006 **in Firefox** and select any colorful story.
3. Open the Vision filter dropdown in the toolbar (the accessibility icon) and step through every option. Each of Deuteranomaly, Deuteranopia, Protanomaly, Protanopia, Tritanomaly, Tritanopia and Achromatopsia should visibly change the canvas colors. Before this PR, only Blurred vision and Grayscale had any effect in Firefox.
4. Choose "Reset color filter" and confirm the canvas returns to normal.
5. Open the same story in isolation (`/iframe.html?id=<story-id>&globals=vision:achromatopsia`) and confirm the filter still applies. This is the behavior #33418 added and it must not regress.
6. Repeat steps 2–4 **in Chrome** and compare against `next`. The filtered colors should look identical to the current behavior, not lighter or washed out. This is the part most worth scrutiny, since it is the intended-invariant rather than the fix itself.
7. Confirm a story that pins `globals: { vision: ... }` still locks the dropdown (from #33599).

Areas most likely to regress: the injected SVG is now rendered rather than `display: none`, so it is worth confirming it introduces no layout shift or stray scrollbar (it is `position: absolute`, 0×0, `overflow: hidden`), and that it produces no new axe violations in the a11y panel (it carries `aria-hidden="true"`).

prs.title: Core: Fix stories failing to load on Windows with the webpack builder
prs.manualTesting:
This needs a Windows machine. It has not been run on Windows with this fix yet; the unit tests simulate the platform.

1. On Windows, create a webpack-based project, for example `npx create-storybook@next --type react --builder webpack5` in a new React project, or take any existing Next.js project that uses `@storybook/nextjs`.
2. With 11.0.0-beta.1, run `npx storybook dev`. Every story shows `Cannot find module './<path>.stories.tsx'`.
3. Install the canary of this PR and run `npx storybook dev` again. The stories render.
4. Run `npx storybook build` and open the static build. The stories render there as well.
